extracted.intended_audience: general readers and literary-minded book/film/TV consumers looking for curated recommendations
extracted.subtask_description: A curated set of short recommendation blurbs for books, films, and TV that explain why a work is worth reading/watching, often linking qualities of form, tone, and reader context to the recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate grab / 'grippiness'
rubrics_metrics.description: Heat makes me less inclined to stick with books that don’t immediately grab me (wait, I think I just figured out what a beach read is).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recommended work should 'immediately grab' the reader — if it fails to hook quickly, the recommender is likely to abandon it. Example: The Nickel Boys is praised as 'utterly gripping.' Anti-pattern: slow starts that don't establish stakes or voice promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative propulsion with emotional impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Propulsive and gorgeous and completely devastating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values forward momentum ('propulsive') combined with stylistic quality ('gorgeous') and strong emotional effect ('devastating'). Used to justify recommending a novel that both moves the reader and delivers emotional weight. Scoring note: measure both pace and affect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of prose / sparseness
rubrics_metrics.description: Funny and strange and perfectly sparse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise for concise, economical writing that still conveys strangeness and humor. Works that are 'perfectly sparse' are recommended for their tonal control and efficiency. Anti-pattern: overwritten, indulgent prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of horror and humor
rubrics_metrics.description: It’s horrific, yes, but the trailer belies how laugh-out-loud funny it is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A work that layers horror with comedy can be especially effective; the interplay can amplify both effects. Example: the film Midsommar is recommended because it is both horrific and funny. Consider tonal balance when recommending horror-adjacent media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtle foreshadowing and implied suspense
rubrics_metrics.description: I tried to remember what it was like to read it for the first time, to not know but also to sense, implicitly (foreshadowing!) what would happen to poor Mrs. Hutchinson...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective use of implicit cues and foreshadowing that lets readers sense future events without explicit spoilers is a valued technique. Works that create that 'sensing' are recommended for their craft in building suspense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Playing with language and form / metafiction
rubrics_metrics.description: It plays with language and form...like all the best metafictional works, it is a story that is also about telling stories—and in this particular case, it manages to engage on yet another level, asking who is allowed to tell stories, and when, and what it costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal experimentation and meta-level inquiry (stories about storytelling, questions of authorship/voice) are strong reasons to recommend a book. Guidance: highlight how form and thematic concerns interact. Example: Carmen Maria Machado's memoir is praised for these qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: High emotional intensity / 'achingly good' quality
rubrics_metrics.description: I was expecting to be good. But I wasn’t expecting it to be this good. I mean, it is achingly good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deep emotional resonance that makes recommending writers describe a work as 'achingly good' is a criterion. Works that move the reader profoundly are prioritized. Example: In the Dream House.

rubrics_metrics.name: Melancholy, quiet devastation, and reflective memory work
rubrics_metrics.description: Melancholy and quietly devastating 2004 novel... as he chops wood, walks his dog, and tends to his property, Trond unpacks memories...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value placed on subdued, elegiac tone and careful handling of memory and grief. Works that unfold inwardly, focusing on small actions and recollection, are recommended for their emotional subtlety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candid, unsparing confessionals on taboo/personal topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Remarkably candid and unsparing debut collection...six powerful, unflinching confessionals...taboos around menstruation and female pain; sexual violence...the grief of miscarriage and infertility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Honesty and willingness to confront taboo or painful subjects candidly is lauded. Recommend memoir/essay collections that are unflinching and brave in subject matter. Example: Emilie Pine's Notes to Self.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention to everyday details and daily rhythms; lyrical essaying
rubrics_metrics.description: Everyday details and daily rhythms receive the most loving attention...an essay collection that weaves between stories of life and death, Renkl’s Alabama childhood, oral histories...the wildlife outside her front door.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Close observation of quotidian life presented lyrically is a quality that merits recommendation. Such writing invites contemplation and often creates strong atmosphere. Example: Late Migrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro-to-macro historical/scholarly synthesis and irony
rubrics_metrics.description: At first glance, this is a lengthy tome...within this apartment building, however, lay the central irony of the revolution—those who believed deeply enough in an idealistic system to embrace violent, repressive means of revolution, were soon enough subjected to those same mechanisms of repression...zoom[s] out to look at the Soviets as just another bunch of millenarians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholarly or historical works that connect intimate detail (apartment-building stories) to large political implications (ironies of revolution) are recommended for their analytic breadth and narrative framing. Guidance: value works that synthesize micro and macro insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eerie atmosphere coupled with precise, piercing language
rubrics_metrics.description: Without a doubt one of the most haunting and beautiful books I have read...the eerie plot will have you turning pages, but the delicate and particular piercing of language will give you pause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation justified by combination of uneasy, haunting atmosphere and carefully chosen, piercing language. Works that sustain mood while offering linguistic precision are especially praised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dense scene-level detail rewarding re-consumption
rubrics_metrics.description: The attention to detail in every scene is wild and you’ll catch things you never saw the first time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works (TV/film/novels) that pack scenes with background detail repay multiple viewings/readings; rewatchability/re-readability is a sign of craft. Recommendation: suggest re-watching/reading to appreciate embedded details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual fit / match recommendations to reader mood or need
rubrics_metrics.description: I recommend the movie Midsommar, particularly if you’ve just been through a breakup...I recommend this book to those who wish to demonstrate their physical strength in public and show off that they can read a giant Russian history book one-handed, but also I recommend this book to everyone, ever, in the world, because it’s so fantastic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations often hinge on reader context (mood, social signaling, time available). Good curator copy identifies which readers or situations will get the most from a work. Anti-pattern: one-size-fits-all endorsements without guidance on who will like it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative recommendation / explicit discouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: I recommend not watching Lost. I tried it out this week, and it’s for the birds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of curatorial practice is to advise against works perceived as low value for certain audiences. Negative recommendations are useful when paired with a brief reason. Guidance: be concise and clear about why a work is discouraged.
